summary: vanexa-agent routes remote-command channel and AI traffic through hardcoded author-controlled Cloudflare Workers
details: The package installs a daemon whose advertised purpose is to receive commands from a paired phone app over WebSocket and execute them on the installer's host (filesystem writes, shell commands, build operations). The shipped bundle hardcodes a relay endpoint at https://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev, a Cloudflare Worker controlled by an account (`hanazaki542`) that does not match the npm publisher (`ikbal_fadilah_vanexa01`). Pairing between phone and desktop traverses this relay rather than being LAN-only as the README diagram implies, so whoever controls the Worker can proxy or inject the network-sourced commands that drive local shell and filesystem execution on the installer's machine. A second hardcoded endpoint at https://vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev is co-located with the documented provider URLs (api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, api.deepseek.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com) and can carry the caller's model prompts and BYOK provider API keys through the same author-controlled infrastructure, contradicting the README's 'No middleman, no subscription' claim. The runtime code is shipped primarily as bytenode-compiled V8 bytecode (dist/bundle.jsc, ~5 MB), recompiled from a 2 MB minified dist/bundle.cjs by a postinstall hook, which obstructs review of the network-to-execute path.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
